## Two process gaps surfaced 2026-06-11 (beekeeper-noted) — gates satisfiable without the work, + reds left for the beekeeper to find

Both are the **FAULT-S4-002 class**: a gate that turns green without the underlying work actually happening. The beekeeper caught two instances in one session.

### Gap 1 — routine red CI checks left for the beekeeper to track down
PR #529 sat with a red `markdown-link-check` (a stale-base artifact) until the beekeeper personally found it. **A routine red check is the agent's to fix autonomously via a fix pass** — only theory-level/substantive failures should surface to the beekeeper. (Captured in memory `feedback-ci-failure-autonomous-fix-pass`.)

### Gap 2 — the tier-3 review gate passes on the LABEL, not on actual reviews (→ FAULT-S4-003)
PR #537 went **ALL-GREEN and self-ticked its CI-green box (notifier #534) with zero reviews run** — because the "Tier-3 review-label required on theory-bearing diffs" check verifies the *label is present*, not that Red Team + Gemini reviews *happened*. The label is applied automatically; so a theory-bearing PR can reach merge-ready with no review having fired. The notifier's self-tick then makes it *look* ready. This is exactly FAULT-S4-002's shape one layer up: the gate is satisfiable without the work.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] **AC1:** Autonomous fix-pass discipline documented in `memory/pr_review_workflow.md` / the review workflow (routine red → fix pass; substantive red → surface). Memory captured; promote to process doc.
- [x] **AC2:** The tier-3 gate verifies real reviews **exist** (a non-notifier comment carrying BOTH a reviewer signature AND a rendered verdict); review **freshness** (reviewed-sha / patch-id vs head) is verified by the **notifier's ALL-GREEN check** — the gate=exists / notifier=fresh division (beekeeper-accepted 2026-06-12; Red Team + Gemini endorsed). A theory PR cannot reach ALL-GREEN without real, current reviews.
- [x] **AC3:** **FAULT-S4-003** logged in `docs/process_violation_log.md` (review gate passed on label alone; #537 reached ALL-GREEN unreviewed).
- [x] **AC4:** Cross-check the interaction with the notifier self-tick (#534) and box-phrasing (#538) — the CI-green self-tick must not imply "reviewed"; the review boxes stay judgment boxes the notifier never ticks (already true, but document the invariant).

## Why it matters
The notifier self-tick (#534) is only safe if the gates it rides are honest. If the tier-3 gate greenlights unreviewed theory diffs, the self-tick amplifies the gap into false "ready" signal. Closing AC2 makes the whole green→self-tick→merge chain trustworthy for theory-bearing work.

Beekeeper-noted 2026-06-11 (PRs #529, #537). Family: #507 (box-gate governance), #538 (box phrasing), FAULT-S4-002 (notifier watcher-tail). Filed by @qbp-oppenheimer.

NOT the trivial `B(μ(e,·))=1` (that only says μ has a left identity). The physically meaningful theorem:

> **`B(f ⋆ g) = B(f) + B(g)`**,  where `(f⋆g)(x) = μ(f(x), g(x))` (pointwise quaternion mult)

— formally showing the substrate's **SU(2) algebra induces the additive topology** of the baryon number. Stepping stone: `B(μ(a,·)) = 1` for any `a` (SU(2) acts on itself preserving charge).

## Full-ledger proof-anchor audit — 17 phantom `provenance_kind:proof` anchors

**Surfaced by:** FAULT-S4-005 Step-3 full-ledger audit (the "extend C3 to full-ledger" extension, beekeeper-directed). First run of the new gate.

### Finding

The Step-3 full-ledger audit scans **all 31 `provenance_kind:proof` anchors** in the CTH ledger (`confluent-trust-inventory-v5_3.v0.3.json`) and checks that each anchor's `proof_file` resolves on `master`. **21 of 31 cite a `proof_file` that 404s.** Two sub-classes:

- **Stale-path (4)** — proof file exists, but the citation uses the old `lean4/QBP/` prefix. Mechanically fixable by correcting the path. Handled in the Step-3 PR (#616). *(PROOF-42zd, PROOF-hessian, PROOF-fano, PROOF-shells → `proofs/Sprint12-Inherited/…`.)*
- **Phantom (17)** — no such file anywhere on `master`. These are the real debt: `provenance_kind:proof` with **no proof file and no `verification` block** (all are `proof_state:written` or have no proof_state at all — none is `verified`). This is the exact #613/#615 class, at scale.

### The 17 phantom anchors

| anchor_id | status | cited (404) proof_file | tracked |
|---|---|---|---|
| INSIGHT-s2-dirac-eta-vanishes | coherent | proofs/QBP/Foundations/QBPHorizonFoundations.lean | #615 |
| DERIV-vaidya-accreting-horizon-spacelike | coherent | proofs/QBP/Foundations/QBPHorizonFoundations.lean | #615 |
| DERIV-hubble-half-entropy-factor | coherent | proofs/QBP/Foundations/QBPHorizonFoundations.lean | #615 |
| PROOF-eigenratios | coherent | lean4/QBP/GaugeBosons.lean | this issue |

| PROOF-3gen | coherent | lean4/QBP/GaugeBosons.lean | this issue |
| PROOF-g2 | coherent | QBP-boundary-cell-model.py | this issue |
| PROOF-alpha-particle-quaternion | coherent | QBP/Cosmo/Nucleosynthesis.lean | this issue |
| PROOF-iron-56-double-octet | coherent | QBP/Cosmo/Nucleosynthesis.lean | this issue |
| PROOF-oxygen-16-sedenion | coherent | QBP/Cosmo/Nucleosynthesis.lean | this issue |
| PROOF-silicon-28-fano-ladder | coherent | QBP/Cosmo/Nucleosynthesis.lean | this issue |
| PROOF-iron-to-ns-bridge | coherent | QBP/Cosmo/DenseMatter.lean | this issue |
| PROOF-seed-mass-from-ln7 | coherent | QBP/Cosmo/SeedMass.lean | this issue |
| PROOF-fano-choice-information | coherent | QBP/Cosmo/FanoChoiceInformation.lean | this issue |
| PRED-btfr-mass-correction | coherent | QBP/Cosmo/RedshiftEvolution.lean | this issue |
| PRED-a0-redshift-linear | marginal | QBP/Cosmo/RedshiftEvolution.lean | this issue |
| FIT-zeta-modulated-profile | marginal | lean4/QBP/SpectralAction/ProfileFit.lean | this issue |

### What this means

None of these 17 was ever verified — no `verification` block, no `proof_state:verified`. They carry `provenance_kind:proof` (and mostly `status:coherent`) on the strength of a proof file that does not exist. **The ledger currently over-claims 17 proven results.** This is a clean negative result: QBP has 17 fewer Lean/Agda-anchored proofs than the ledger asserted.

### Resolution options (per anchor — theory-state, oppenheimer + cth call)

1. **Prove it** — write the cited proof, verify it (`proof_state:verified` + `verification` block), and the anchor resolves. Register entry drops.
2. **Reclassify** — if the result is a derivation/insight/prediction rather than a machine-checked proof, change `provenance_kind: proof → theory|derivation`, drop the proof claim, keep the physics on its actual footing. Register entry drops.

### Gate posture (Step-3 PR #616)

The full-ledger audit ships as a **hard gate** protecting going forward: any *new* `provenance_kind:proof` anchor whose `proof_file` doesn't resolve is blocked immediately. The 17 known phantoms are enumerated in a **shrink-only, issue-linked remediation register** (`docs/cth/proof-anchor-remediation.json`) — the register can only lose entries (as anchors are proved or reclassified), never gain them silently, and each entry must carry a tracking issue. This is materially different from the FAULT-S4-005 baseline that was defeated by a *silent CI-driven raise*: a register add is a visible, reviewed commit.

**Ask:** @qbp-oppenheimer (theory) + @cth-implementor (schema/ledger) to adjudicate each of the 17 — prove vs reclassify — as frozen-theory remediation. This is exactly the kind of over-claim the FAULT-S4-005 remediation exists to burn down.

Refs FAULT-S4-005 · #613 · #615 · #616 · #464

## Connect the orphan proofs back to the CTH — 1×1 validation, one large PR

**Owner:** @qbp-oppenheimer (theory-state) · **Beekeeper-directed** · **Process:** `docs/cth/proof-anchor-best-practices.md`

The under-claim mirror of the over-claim burn-down (#617/#615/#613). The audit found **576 orphan theorems** — proven in `proofs/**/*.lean`, cited by **no** CTH anchor — across **30 files, every one sorry-free and native_decide-free** (real kernel-verified proof). A crude split puts **~100 as load-bearing results** (the #474 operations-complete cell-matrix: `Breakdown.lean` ✗-cells incl. the 42, `TowerLaws`/`OctonionLaws`/`CrossProduct` ✓-cell laws, the experiment predictions) vs ~470 genuine auxiliary lemmas.

### The task (the discipline)

Go through **every orphan, one by one** — do **not** batch-judge by file. For each theorem:

1. **Validate** whether it is *meaningfully* a CTH-worthy result (a load-bearing QBP claim the ledger should carry) or an auxiliary lemma (a step in a larger proof, correctly unanchored).
2. **If meaningfully connected:** add a `provenance_kind:proof` anchor that cites it and meets the **C3-FULL evidence bar** — `proof_state:verified` + a language-clean `verification.axiom_closure` (capture `#print axioms` / `--safe`) + `sorry_count:0` + the resolving proof_file. Because the proofs are already clean, a correct anchor clears the bar immediately — this is *recovering* proven work, not re-proving.
3. **If not connected:** state **clearly and per-theorem why not** — e.g. "auxiliary lemma supporting `<result>`", "coordinate/plumbing", "subsumed by anchored `<anchor_id>`". The reason is the artifact; a bare "skip" is not acceptable.

Every one of the 576 gets an explicit disposition — **anchored, or a stated reason.** No silent skips.

### Deliverable

**One large PR** carrying the whole pass: the new anchors + a per-theorem disposition record (a manifest / table mapping each orphan → anchored `id` or reason-not). This becomes the ledger's honest statement of what QBP has actually proven.

### Orphan clusters (starting map; full list in `scripts/anchor_inverse_audit.py --out-json`)

| orphans | ~result | file |
|---:|---:|---|
| 26 | 18 | `Foundations/Breakdown.lean` — ✗-cells incl. the 42 |
| 55 | 17 | `Foundations/OctonionLaws.lean` — 𝕆 ✓-cell laws |
| 49 | 15 | `Foundations/TowerLaws.lean` — ℝ ✓-cell laws |
| 27 | 16 | `Foundations/CDLifting.lean` |
| 37 | 11 | `Foundations/CrossProduct.lean` |
| … | … | 25 more files (Exp 65, CDAlg 44 — mostly auxiliary) |

### After this lands (process phase 2, separate)

Once the ledger reflects the true anchored set, convert the orphan ratchet (`lean_side_orphans`, currently still a tolerated count — PATTERN-02) into an **absolute manifest-based under-claim gate**: a declared anchor-worthy proof not cited by its anchor is a HARD FAIL. Tracked here as the follow-on; the best-practice doc already commits to it.

Refs FAULT-S4-007 · #474 · #616 · #617 · #615 · #613

## Summary

`scripts/check_layer_imports.py` Rule-3 (aggregator-completeness) only covers `QBP/Foundations/**` — it does **not** cover the physics directories (`QBP/Experiments/**`, `QBP/Optics/**`, `QBP/Units/**`, `Sprint12-Inherited/**`). As a result, a Lean file that is not root-imported into `QBP.lean` (or its aggregators) can be **build-invisible**: it compiles nowhere in CI, so a broken proof in it is never caught.

## How it surfaced (#619)

During the #619 orphan-anchoring sweep, `QBP/Experiments/General3D.lean` was found to be **both build-broken and build-invisible**:
- It had an unclosed goal (`prob_up_general` after `rw [expectation_general]`) — fixed with `ring`.
- It was not imported from `QBP.lean`, so CI never compiled it. The break had been latent.

Fixed reactively in the #619 branch (added `import QBP.Experiments.General3D` + `AngleDependent` to `QBP.lean`, plus the `ring`), but the **gate that should have caught it does not cover physics dirs** — so the next build-invisible physics file will slip through the same way.

## Proposed fix

Extend `check_layer_imports.py` Rule-3 aggregator-completeness to enforce that every `.lean` under the physics/prediction dirs is transitively root-reachable from `QBP.lean` (or an explicitly-allowlisted non-root file), mirroring the Foundations coverage. Add an adversarial test (plant an unreferenced physics file, assert the gate flags it) per the gate-validation discipline in `docs/cth/proof-anchor-best-practices.md` ("a gate is judged by what it catches").

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] **AC1:** Rule-3 (or an equivalent check) flags any `.lean` under `QBP/Experiments/`, `QBP/Optics/`, `QBP/Units/`, `Sprint12-Inherited/` that is not transitively imported by `QBP.lean`/`QBPSprint12` roots.
- [x] **AC2:** An adversarial test plants a build-invisible physics file and asserts the gate catches it.
- [x] **AC3:** Running the extended gate on the current tree passes (no currently-orphaned build-invisible files remain, or they are explicitly allowlisted with rationale).

## Lane / labels
Lane: qbp-implementor (CI-gate scripts). Type: `type: infra`. Sprint: House Keeping.
Surfaced by: #619 orphan-anchoring.

## Summary

CI's Lean build step runs bare `lake build` (`.github/workflows/lean-foundations.yml`), which compiles only the `@[default_target]`s — the `QBP` and `QBPSprint12` lean_libs. The two `lean_exe` targets are **not** default targets, so CI never compiles them:

- `lean_exe «oracle»` (root `QBP.Oracle.Main`) → `QBP/Oracle/Main.lean`, `QBP/Oracle/FloatCompute.lean`
- `lean_exe «gen_test_vectors»` (root `QBP.Units.GenTestVectors`) → `QBP/Units/GenTestVectors.lean`, `QBP/Units/Oracle.lean`

A broken proof/def in any of these would ride CI-green — the same build-invisibility class the #625 gate exists to close, but for files reachable only via an exe target rather than a lib.

Surfaced by #625: the build-visibility gate defines "visible" as reachable from a **default-target** root (matching what CI actually compiles). These 5 files are therefore quarantined in `proofs/QBP/.build-visibility-quarantine.json` (FFI separately under #644 — it's reachable from no target at all).

## Fix options
1. **Add the exe targets to CI's build** — `lake build oracle gen_test_vectors` alongside the default `lake build` (cheapest; keeps them non-default but CI-compiled).
2. **Promote the exes to `@[default_target]`** — makes bare `lake build` compile them (as #482 did for the Sprint12 lib).

Either makes the exe corpus CI-compiled; the #625 gate then sees them as visible and the quarantine entries are removed as stale (shrink-only).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] **AC:** CI compiles `QBP/Oracle/Main.lean`, `QBP/Oracle/FloatCompute.lean`, `QBP/Units/GenTestVectors.lean`, `QBP/Units/Oracle.lean` (a planted break in any fails CI).
- [x] **AC:** The corresponding `.build-visibility-quarantine.json` entries are removed (gate stays green with them gone).

## Lane / labels
Lane: qbp-implementor (CI build config). Type: `type: infra`. Sprint: House Keeping. Surfaced-by: #625.

body:
## Summary

`AXIOM-1.kill_condition[0]` (question 1, encoded at #659; ledger 6.1.0 → 6.2.0) is **defective in both directions**, found by the rule-flow research conversation (#635 Phase B) and confirmed by its heterogeneous confirmer (`docs/foundations/rule-flow-research-conversation-confirmer-verdict-2026-09-20.md` §3, on branch `foundations/rule-flow`, PR #667). **This issue records the defect; it rules nothing.** The rewrite is a constitutional edit to an axiom's kill text — a Tier-3 PR of its own, after the beekeeper decides it should proceed.

## The text (verbatim, 6.1.0)

> KILL — a proven flow on StateSphere (the rule, #635) whose omega-limit set meets the zero-divisor locus and whose omega-limit map is non-injective on a set of states of positive normalised surface measure on StateSphere … DISCHARGE — the same flow proven information-preserving (omega-limit map injective almost everywhere with respect to that measure). First-order semiflows are injective at finite time, so the criterion is on the omega-limit, not on finite-time states.

## Defect 1 — the DISCHARGE clause is satisfiable only by the zero flow

The omega-limit map ω is constant along flow lines. By the flow-box theorem and Fubini, on any set of positive measure inside the regular set {F ≠ 0}, ω is non-injective. The regular set has full measure here (the rest-point set is the zero set of a non-trivial polynomial map; measured 0/5000). Hence:

> **"ω-limit map injective almost everywhere" ⟺ almost every point is a rest point ⟺ the flow is trivial.**

Four readings were tested (full-measure set; null failure set; measure-class on ω_*μ; injective modulo the flow) — all fail; the last is refuted by a measurement: dω has rank 8 with a 6-dimensional fibre at a generic point (the crystal manifold is 8-dimensional; hosting-definition Hessian rank 6 transverse). The clause's own parenthetical shows the drafter knew finite-time injectivity; infinite-time non-injectivity follows from the same semiflow property. **No non-trivial flow can ever earn this discharge.**

## Defect 2 — the KILL's first conjunct carries no measure qualifier

Grammatically the measure qualifier attaches only to the second conjunct. The zero-divisor locus is non-empty on StateSphere and consists entirely of rest points (max ‖F‖ = 2.2e-15 over 300 locus points; candidate theorem `ruleField_eq_zero_of_potential_eq_one`). For s₀ on the locus, ω(s₀) = {s₀} ⊆ locus. So, read literally, **the kill fires the instant local existence of the flow is proved** — on a triviality with no physics in it. Under the charitable reading (qualifier on both conjuncts), conjunct 1 fails from below (a trajectory from V < 1 never reaches V = 1 — candidate theorem `omega_avoids_locus`, given monotonicity) and conjunct 2 is automatic, so the kill cannot fire and the discharge cannot be earned: **question 1 is frozen either way.**

## The physics objection (Sabine overlay)

Non-injectivity of the infinite-time limit map is not a symptom of information destruction; it is the definition of dissipation. An overdamped gradient flow forgets its initial condition by construction. Used as AXIOM-1's test, this criterion would kill the axiom on every damped system in physics — the criterion tests the wrong thing.

## What is NOT decided here

Which replacement wording is right. A concretely nameable candidate exists (negate conjunct 1 with a measure qualifier: *discharged if the flow is proven to have ω(s) ∩ zero-divisor-locus = ∅ for a set of s of full measure*), but choosing the criterion for an axiom's kill is a scope/constitutional decision (§10: wicked — no stopping rule), not a theorem. Nothing on this issue puts a physical choice to the beekeeper; it asks for the process decision **whether** a rewrite PR proceeds.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1:** A Tier-3 PR rewrites `AXIOM-1.kill_condition[0]` through the confined writer with a measure qualifier on both conjuncts and a discharge clause satisfiable by some non-trivial flow, citing this issue and the confirmer verdict; Red Team → Gemini → §I4 (@qbp-architecture, decision-boundary coherence) → schema co-sign (@cth-implementor). — **MET:** PR #687 (merged 92becf1, ledger 6.11.0): confined writer declares AXIOM-1 only; both conjuncts measure-qualified (positive measure w.r.t. the working ensemble / full-measure discharge); discharge earnable by the postulated non-trivial flow; cites #668 + the 2026-09-20 confirmer verdict; Red Team APPROVE (issuecomment-5836219913), Gemini APPROVE ×3, §I4 qbp-architecture (live-test seq 1700, carries to 87cea1f), schema cth-implementor (seq 1702, carries; post-merge verification clean seq 1834).
- [x] **AC2:** The candidate theorems the rewrite leans on (`potential_le_normForm_sq`, `ruleField_eq_zero_of_potential_eq_one`, `potential_antitone_along_flow`, `omega_avoids_locus`) are proved before the rewrite is encoded (prove-before-encode), or the rewrite is worded not to depend on them. — **MET:** all four theorems PROVED on master in `proofs/QBP/Substrate/RuleFlow.lean` before the encode (0 sorry; `omega_avoids_locus`/`omega_avoids_zeroDivisors` anchored as PROOF-rule-descent-avoids-zero-divisors); the kill text cites them as the discharge route, conditional on flow existence which is honestly left OPEN.
- [x] **AC3:** `FLAG-rule-flow-open` (sync PR #665) updated to point at this issue as the tracked defect. — **MET:** `FLAG-rule-flow-open.notes` appended in the same transaction (a312fcb → 87cea1f): records that AXIOM-1's discharge rides on this tracker, names #668 and PR #687, describes the new KILL/DISCHARGE mechanics; `AXIOM-1.discharge` field = FLAG-rule-flow-open (bidirectional link).

Refs #635, #647 (trigger issue), #659 (the encode), #667 (Phase A/B records). Does not close any of them.

**Parent:** #473 (substrate). **Named as missing by:** substrate first draft v0.1 §4 and §8 (PR #685, "no issue"), the #473 plan §4, the Strategy-C checkpoint §5.1 (PR #553, 2026-09-28). **Filed** 2026-09-28 at the beekeeper's direction ("file it").

## The gap
Everything proved about the in-flight region {V > 0} of the state sphere is **negative or structural**: V's first-order data constrains at most one of 14 tangent directions (none at rest points, including the frozen ridge); every functional of V's level-set topology is rule-blind; the hosting identity s(sx) = −N(s)x fails at every in-flight state (anchors: `PROOF-in-flight-first-order-data-constrains-at-most-one-direction`, `PROOF-level-set-invariants-rule-blind`, `PROOF-hosting-identity-fails-in-flight`, `PROOF-vacuum-sublocale-v-natural`, `PROOF-sublevel-infimum-rule-independent`). **No positive account exists**: nothing on record says what the in-flight region *is* as a space with configurations — the "pointless" half of #473 AC1 (c) ("the in-flight regime where points are not yet available is covered"). Consequence downstream: the substrate yields no spatial primitive, so Strategy C's `∫d³x` circularity (#553 §5.1, W1) is relocated, not removed; a *fundamental* C cannot start.

## The question
Give a **definition, not a description**, of the in-flight region as a space with configurations, consistent with the proved negatives above. v0.1 §4 names three candidates:
1. the orbit space of the rule (needs #635: existence of the flow, `FLAG-rule-flow-open`);
2. a locale / condensed object (the reopened route, `FLAG-locale-forcing-route-reopened`; Prop 13(b) is its kill; #661's T2 is the negative direction);
3. a limit of finite approximations (e.g. the CD index tower's profinite structure — but attack 4 (#678) found it inert: every continuous profinite action on 𝕊 has finite image).

## Summary
Prove the two-line Substrate-side bridge lemma `gradVof = RuleFlow.gradV` (Foundations copy of the closed-form gradient = the rule's gradient), then re-scope ledger anchor `PROOF-gradient-lies-in-host-kernel-algebra` (anchor 4 of PR #689) and re-add its withheld chain edge. Split out of housekeeping issue #683 (one checkbox there) on qbp-architecture's request (live-test seq 2108) so the citations in the ledger and the #688 doc point at an issue that tracks exactly this and nothing else.

## Context
- `proofs/QBP/Foundations/InFlightAlgebra.lean` defines `gradVlo`, `gradVhi`, `gradVof` as **verbatim copies** of the right-hand sides of `RuleFlow.gradV`'s CD components (header l.546–548 states the intended identities `gradVlo s = cdLo (gradV s)`, `gradVhi s = cdHi (gradV s)`; textually verified only, issue #688 Lean interlude, 14b8160).
- The Foundations layer cannot import Substrate (`check_layer_imports.py`), so the identity has to live in `proofs/QBP/Substrate/` (RuleFlow.lean or a new `RuleFlowBridge.lean`), where `RuleFlow.gradV` (RuleFlow.lean:306) and its component lemma (l.312) are in scope.
- Consumers of the gap today (all say "OPEN, #683"): anchor 4's `name`/`description` NOT-claimed clause; anchor 4's `prediction_chain` = `[PROOF-alternator-vanishes-iff-commute]` only — the edge to `PROOF-rule-gradient-and-tangent-field` was withheld (§I4 R2, cth chain-liveness, PR #689); `docs/foundations/688-in-flight-definition-2026-09-29.md` §1 PROVED row, §2 group-free route (ARGUMENT), §5 K-a / S4 rows, §6 gradV row, §9 OPEN row.
- Under the criticality-metric edge rules converged 2026-09-30 (live-test seq 2074–2086), the re-added edge is a legitimate **Substrate → Substrate / Foundations derivation** (target-layer ≤ source-layer), so it is countable once it exists; the bridge lemma itself is a Substrate theorem with Foundations targets.

## Requirements
- Substrate-side theorems, kernel-checked, axioms ⊆ {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, no `sorry`, no `native_decide`:
  - `theorem gradVlo_eq_cdLo_gradV (s : CDAlg ℝ 4) : Foundations.InFlightAlgebra.gradVlo s = cdLo (RuleFlow.gradV s)`
  - `theorem gradVhi_eq_cdHi_gradV (s : CDAlg ℝ 4) : Foundations.InFlightAlgebra.gradVhi s = cdHi (RuleFlow.gradV s)`
  - `theorem gradVof_eq_gradV (s : CDAlg ℝ 4) : Foundations.InFlightAlgebra.gradVof s = RuleFlow.gradV s` (the packaged form; expected `rfl` or `ext` + the two above)
  - corollary in Substrate: `RuleFlow.gradV s ∈ 𝕆_s` (`InKernelAlgebra s (gradV s)`) and `α • s + β • gradV s ∈ 𝕆_s`, by rewriting through the bridge.
- Bounded build from `proofs/` (`run-bounded 6G 1800 taskset -c 3-5 lake build QBP.Substrate.<module>`), `#print axioms` for each new theorem, both gates (`check_lean_foundations.py`, `check_layer_imports.py`) exit 0.
- Ledger (confined writer only, Tier-3 PR): anchor 4 `PROOF-gradient-lies-in-host-kernel-algebra` — move "gradVof = RuleFlow.gradV" from the NOT-claimed clause into the claimed clause with the new witnesses; re-add `PROOF-rule-gradient-and-tangent-field` to `prediction_chain`; re-stamp `verification`. No other anchor changes. Inverse-anchor ratchet via encode-on-PR, not a baseline bump.
- Doc: `docs/foundations/688-in-flight-definition-2026-09-29.md` — §1 PROVED row, §2 group-free route (ARGUMENT → PROVED for the P2 rule's *pointwise* containment; flow existence stays OPEN under `FLAG-rule-flow-open`), §5 K-a / S4 qualifiers, §6 gradV row, §9 OPEN row: replace "OPEN, #683" with the theorem names. Do NOT touch the flow-existence / leaf-invariance claims: those remain conditional on `FLAG-rule-flow-open`.
- Untick the bridge checkbox on issue #683 and point it here (done at filing).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] **AC1:** the three bridge theorems (+ the Substrate corollary) exist, kernel-checked, standard axioms only, in a Substrate-layer module; `check_layer_imports.py` exit 0. — **met** (PR #691 @ `5a095aa`): `proofs/QBP/Substrate/RuleFlowBridge.lean`, 5 theorems (`gradVlo_eq_cdLo_gradV`, `gradVhi_eq_cdHi_gradV`, `gradVof_eq_gradV`, `gradV_mem_kernelAlgebra`, `smul_self_add_smul_gradV_mem_kernelAlgebra`), `#print axioms` ⊆ {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, 0 sorry; `check_layer_imports.py` exit 0; independent clean builds by the Red Team (issuecomment-5918526831) and qbp-architecture (issuecomment-5919321688, 3129/3129 jobs); CI `lake build (zero errors)` pass.
- [x] **AC2:** anchor 4 re-encoded via the confined writer: identity moved into the claimed clause, chain edge `PROOF-rule-gradient-and-tangent-field` re-added, `root_audit.py` / `check_anchor_manifest.py` / `anchor_inverse_audit.py --check` / jsonschema all exit 0; anchors 1–3 of PR #689 unchanged except `verification.verifier` if the shared constant re-stamps. — **met as amended** (amendment comment on this issue, 2026-09-30; import-direction edge rule): new Substrate anchor `PROOF-rule-gradient-lies-in-host-kernel-algebra` (chain S→F + S→S), anchor 4 byte-identical to master except its NOT-claimed pointer, chain F-only; `root_audit.py` / `check_anchor_manifest.py` / `anchor_inverse_audit.py --check` / jsonschema all exit 0 (Red Team re-check issuecomment-5919115591 re-ran them); anchors 1–3 of PR #689 untouched; ledger 6.13.0/344, manifest 105. cth schema co-sign APPROVE (issuecomment-5919230517).
- [x] **AC3:** every "#683" bridge citation in the #688 doc and in anchor 4 replaced by the theorem names; the flow-existence claims are NOT upgraded (still `FLAG-rule-flow-open`). — **met**: every "#683" bridge citation in `docs/foundations/688-in-flight-definition-2026-09-29.md` and in anchor 4 replaced by the theorem names / the new anchor id (Red Team re-check table rows 5–5e, no live "OPEN, #683" bridge citation); flow-existence and leaf-invariance claims NOT upgraded (`FLAG-rule-flow-open` intact; verified by Red Team, Gemini and §I4).

## Notes
- Two-line by construction: the Foundations definitions were written as verbatim copies, so `rfl` (or `simp [gradVlo_def, RuleFlow.cdLo_gradV]`) is the expected proof; if it is not `rfl`, the discrepancy is itself a finding to report (textual verification was the only check).

**Rung: engineering.** DoD per the Acceptance & Verification Standard §1.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **AC1 (encoder).** The confined encode scripts write `proof_assistants` only from `inter/notary-evidence/` records.
- **AC2 (no hand edits).** CI recomputes PA with the CTH engine at the pinned ledger version and fails on any difference from the committed value.
- **AC3 (honest backfill).** All 147 proof/derivation anchors get a computed PA. Expected spot values, all on **existing anchor ids**:
  - `PROOF-hessian` = **0**: native_decide only, and no `verification` block (one of the 23 without one);
  - one clean Lean-only proof = **1**: name the id in the PR;
  - one unmechanized derivation = **0**;
  - `PROOF-cd-structure-constant-tables` = **2** once the Notary's Fano Coq-port evidence lands, and **1** until then. The PR states which applies at merge time.

  The PA-2 *logic* is also tested on a synthetic two-evidence fixture (`testdata/pa/`), so it doesn't depend on that run. *(Amended 2026-10-01: the earlier "#575's intertwiner = 2" named no QBP anchor, since that result exists only as Notary evidence (cycle 6), and an AC with no referent can't be falsified. Caught by @qbp-oppenheimer. Anchoring the intertwiner is a separate decision.)*
- **AC4 (anti-weakening).** No anchor's PA rises without a new evidence record, and every drop is listed in the PR's before/after table.
- **AC5 (display).** The PA badge renders on anchor displays: local and effective, with the assistant names.

**Coverage matrix** (`scripts/test_pa_ledger.py` + the CI job `pa-reconcile`)
| AC | Test | Mutation that must make it fail | Boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1 | `test_encoder_reads_evidence_only` | let the encoder accept a `--pa` argument | unit |
| AC2 | CI `pa-reconcile` on a planted hand edit (PA 1→2, no evidence) | make the reconcile job warn instead of fail | CI |
| AC3 | `test_backfill_spot_values` (hessian=0, a named clean-Lean id=1, a named derivation=0, Fano = 1 or 2 per landed evidence) + `test_pa2_from_two_evidence_fixture` (synthetic) | default missing evidence to 1; count one evidence record twice | unit, on the real ledger + fixture |
| AC4 | `test_no_silent_pa_rise`, `test_drops_listed` | allow a rise without evidence; suppress the drop table | unit |
| AC5 | `test_badge_render` (golden) | render `pa_count` in place of `pa_effective` | unit (golden) |

**Seam:** QBP CI calls the CTH engine from the confluent-trust issue (pinned version). An engine change must be re-vendored, or `pa-reconcile` fails.

**Verification boundary:** CI proves the ledger agrees with the engine on committed evidence. It does not prove the evidence is true; that's the notary issue's re-execution (AC5).

Owners: @qbp-oppenheimer (writer), @qbp-implementor (gate). Depends on the confluent-trust and notary issues.

body:
**Spike.** Time-boxed, disposable, ends in an answer. Per the ratified forging method §3: probe code is thrown away and only the finding is kept. Search-before-file: \`gh issue list --search "dependency closure tool spike"\` returned no match.

**Director / owner: @qbp-oppenheimer** (QBP#696's owner; single director). **Capacity: @deming** nods before anything builds. **Reviewer of the answer: @qbp-architecture.**

## Why
The root-cause analysis on QBP#698 found that the staleness closure's edge cases share one cause. We **re-implement module resolution with regexes** (Lake, Agda), which is a load-bearing *float*. The proposed fix is to **derive each prover's import closure from its own dependency tool** at the pinned commit. Before committing to that, we need to know whether it works.

## The question (one, explicit)
For a QBP anchor's \`proof_file\` at a **pinned commit**, can each prover's own tool return the **transitive closure of same-repo source files** it imports, **deterministically**, **without a full Mathlib build**, and at an acceptable CI cost?

| Prover | Candidate tool | Must answer |
|---|---|---|
| Lean 4 / Lake | \`lean --deps\` under \`lake env\`, or Lake's own resolution | Does it resolve both lake libraries (\`QBP\`, \`QBPSprint12\` bare roots) from a checkout at the pin, without building Mathlib oleans? Do QBP-local modules come out as file paths? |
| Agda | \`agda --dependency-graph\` (or \`--only-scope-checking\`) | Does it resolve every same-repo root from the \`.agda-lib\` files, including \`private open import\` and cross-root imports? |
| Coq | \`coqdep\` with the \`_CoqProject\` \`-Q\`/\`-R\` mappings | Same question, for when a Coq proof lives in-repo. Today Coq evidence is cross-repo (notary), so this is forward-looking. |

## Done = the question answered, in writing
A short finding on this issue:
- per tool: works / doesn't / partially;
- exact command, wall time, RAM and disk at the pin;
- determinism: the same output twice, and **across checkouts**;
- whether the output for the 4 known-moved anchors at QBP master \`516dfcb\` matches QBP#698's closures: \`PROOF-hessian\` (S includes \`Sedenion.lean\`) and the 3 Agda anchors. The Fano keys \`6b972a7d\` / \`0f32f714\` must reproduce.

**Required output (Governing Principle 1):** a capability-gap list feeding the decision on QBP#696:
- **tools work:** rewrite #696 on the tools and delete the parser;
- **they don't:** merge QBP#698 with the root-cause analysis recorded as the reason we accept it.

## Bounds
- **Time-box:** half a day.

## Why
The `pr-check-status` notifier posts a "🟢 Tech-green — review-ready" comment on every Tier-3 PR with a four-item checklist (Red Team / Gemini / Synthesis + fix rounds / Human Visual Review) that it **never ticks**. On PR #705 the beekeeper read those boxes as open review work although the PR body (the record) had every leg ticked with evidence and the Tier-3 review gate had already detected the review artifact and gone green. The beekeeper's direction (2026-10-15): *"I do not want to be misinformed, there is enough complicated stuff going on I need clarity."* A machine comment that contradicts the record is noise at the merge gate.

**Search before filing** (`gh issue list --state open --search` on "notifier checklist", "review-ready checklist", "pr-check-status", "tech-green"): no existing issue. Owner: @qbp-implementor (owns `.github/workflows/pr-check-status.yml`); filed by qbp-oppenheimer with the beekeeper's go.

## Deliverable
`.github/workflows/pr-check-status.yml` (notifier job): when upserting the verdict comment, derive the checklist state from the same evidence the Tier-3 gate uses —
- **Red Team** ticked iff a non-notifier comment on the PR contains a Red Team signature (`Red Team|Sabine|Grothendieck|Knuth`) **and** a verdict (`APPROVE|APPROVE-WITH-CONCERN|REQUEST CHANGES|BLOCKING|DEFER`) in the same comment (the `check_tier3_label.py` rule);
- **Gemini** ticked iff the same for `Gemini|Furey|Feynman`;
- **Synthesis + fix rounds** ticked iff the latest `<!-- reviewed-sha -->` marker's patch-id equals the head's (the freshness rule the notifier already computes) — or drop this row, since it is not a gate;
- **Human Visual Review** left for the beekeeper, with one explicit line: "The PR body is the record; this checklist mirrors detected review artifacts."
- A carried-review comment (re-land case, as PR #705) counts the same as a fresh review.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] **AC1:** on a PR whose comments carry Red Team + Gemini artifacts, the notifier's checklist shows those two rows ticked; on a PR with none, unticked. Tested with the workflow's fixture/comment-boundary mechanism; mutant "always unticked" and "always ticked" both KILLED.
- [x] **AC2:** the comment states that the PR body is the record.
- [x] **AC3:** no change to any gate's pass/fail logic (the notifier is informational); `check_tier3_label.py` untouched.

Refs #705 (the mis-read), #702, #481 (Tier-3 gate origin), `docs/workflows/review_tiers.md`.

## Summary

Beekeeper-directed (2026-10-17, live-test seq 2914–2931 + direct): QBP's facility design docs, the "Academic Steampunk → Solarpunk" design system, and the Paget / Bio-Symmetry Design Group personas are repurposed as the **craft family's shared Port**, stewarded by hutchins (craft-implementor). QBP retains construction of its own experiment/test spaces and the **Engine Cartographer** persona as the interface.

Searched open issues first (QBP + craft: "port / craft / pointer / hutchins / facility"): no existing issue. #393 (facility exterior build) is the adjacent housekeeping item and stays open — its scope moves to the Port steward's call.

## Beekeeper framing (verbatim intent)

> your team will produce a set of specs and interfaces that are needed from the port for each experiment space, with an expectation Hutchins will have to tell you where to "plug in" the experiment.

hutchins's working read (seq 2916), ratified by qbp-architecture (seq 2929): **spec-first** — a test unit is a declarative, versioned spec the Port renders in the shared design system; Kaiju-scene-load stays as an escape hatch for bespoke geometry; the Engine Cartographer authors/validates the spec QBP-side.

## Hand-off conditions (agreed seq 2915/2916; ratified seq 2929)

- (a) **Per-file provenance** travels with every ported file: origin repo + commit, authors as supported by git history, Bio-Symmetry Design Group byline where the file carries it.
- (b) **One canonical home per artefact via a commit pair**: craft PR #2 imports at QBP master `18ec30e`; QBP PR #712 keeps full text with pointer headers + flips the persona-registry rows. Experiment-space code (`src/bakeoff/kaiju/game/`) stays canonical in QBP (craft dropped `port/kaiju/` at `4846aae`).
- **Visibility** (beekeeper ruling, seq 2923/2929): canonical copy is private in craft for now; craft goes public once the Port is working (tracked as craft#3); QBP keeps the full-text public record.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — Pointer headers on `docs/design-system.md`, `docs/design/facility_location.md`, `docs/design/facility_exterior/paget_concept.md`, `docs/design/facility_central_hub.md`, `docs/design/micro_interior_hallway.md`: canonical home = craft `port/...` @ import sha; canonical private-in-craft-for-now statement; full text retained; provenance block.
- [ ] AC2 — `docs/personas/README.md` + `docs/personas/paget.md`: Paget + 6 specialists marked "ported to craft @ <sha>"; Engine Cartographer retained as QBP's interface persona with its canonical remit stated in README.md.
- [ ] AC3 — `docs/design/port-experiment-interface.md`: versioned template for what QBP needs from the Port per experiment space + the `PlugIn` record the Port returns + instance zero = the double-slit lab. Draft for hutchins's review as Port steward.
- [ ] AC4 — Craft import PR cross-referenced (link + sha + path) in the QBP PR body.
- [ ] AC5 — `src/bakeoff/kaiju/` untouched; `src/viz/theme.py` / `src/viz/interactive/src/theme.h` stay canonical in QBP as build inputs (craft copies are snapshots).
- [ ] AC6 — **Merge order + sha bump:** craft PR #2 merges first (beekeeper); then one commit on #712 bumps the import sha to craft's merge sha (owner: qbp-oppenheimer; trigger: hutchins's merge ping); then #712 merges. If #712 merges first, the bump is a follow-up PR referencing this issue.

## Plan

1. PR #712 (branch `docs/craft-port-pointers`) carries AC1–AC5.
2. Review cycle: Red Team → Gemini → §I4 (qbp-architecture coherence; hutchins as Port steward on the interface doc). Merge is the beekeeper's.
3. AC6 on craft PR #2 landing.
4. Follow-ups (separate issues, QBP-side, owner Engine Cartographer via qbp-oppenheimer): `docs/design/spaces/03-double-slit.md` as the first versioned space spec; a PlugIn record request to the steward for it.

Owner: qbp-oppenheimer. Steward of the Port: hutchins (craft). Bridge thread: live-test seq 2914–2931.
